title: NVIDIA Kumo Tabular Sets a New Accuracy-Efficiency Frontier for Tabular Prediction
article_summary: NVIDIA has released Kumo Tabular, an open-source tabular foundation model that predicts labels for new data rows using a single in-context forward pass without per-dataset training. The model, available in sizes ranging from 28M to 215M parameters, is pretrained exclusively on synthetic tables generated from random structural causal models to handle missing values and complex distributions. It utilizes an architecture featuring cell-group tokens with Fourier-feature embeddings and alternating column and row attention mechanisms to maintain efficiency. NVIDIA claims the model achieves state-of-the-art results on benchmarks like TabArena and BeyondArena, offering significantly faster runtime than competitors like LimiX-2. The model is released under the OpenMDW-1.1 license, with weights and a structured-data-models library available on Hugging Face and GitHub.
